messages:
maria: Heads-up — customer 375 (Dedicated + private control plane) is blocked: control-plane-admin role failing KMS decrypt for tenant secrets after RBAC refactor.
ryan: Ack. Repro steps?
maria: From their onprem env: calls to /v1/private/keys/decrypt return 403. Error in logs: "permission denied: kms:Decrypt". We saw this after the role rename (controlplane:admin -> controlplane:supervisor) merged last night.
alex.k: That rename should've been covered by the role-alias table migration. Did the migration run for private control planes?
maria: Migration job claimed success but the audit shows bindings still referencing old role name for org 375. suspect a race between migration job and allowlist sync.
jenni: sec-bot log shows a binding create event at 1719898000, then a role prune at 1719901000. Maybe prune removed the alias before bind completed.
sec-bot: automated-alert: role-prune skipped safety-check for "controlplane:admin" -> legacy-binding detected in dedicated/private namespaces.
ryan: Two hypotheses: 1) role aliasing table not replicated to private control plane replicas; 2) VPC allowlist prevented control-plane from calling KMS endpoint (egress IP mismatch).
alex.k: Repro attempt from staging private control plane: `curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://private.cp.local/v1/kms/decrypt` => 403 with same policy message. Locally, admin-account can decrypt.
maria: I captured the IAM policy JSON attached by customer: "Effect": "Deny", "Action": "kms:Decrypt", "Condition": {"StringNotEquals": {"aws:SourceVpc": "vpc-1234"}} — but our service account should be using the allowed VPC. mismatch in source VPC seen.
jenni: Do we map service account traffic through the same egress NAT as customer workload in private deployments? There was a change to egress-proxy last quarter.
ryan: Not always — dedicated/private control plane pods sometimes route via host-network or a different NAT; that change could break source-vpc check.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolled back egress-proxy change in canary on 1719895000 due to unrelated test failure.
alex.k: So we have both an alias/bind race and egress IP drift. Which is primary? customer logs show explicit kms:Decrypt denial with SourceVpc mismatch first, then role not found after retries.
maria: Quick mitigation: 1) add temporary allowlist entry for the control-plane egress IPs in customer KMS policy (manual) 2) revert the role-prune in the migration for private environments and re-run alias sync with locks.
ryan: I can do 1) with ops oncall if customer approves. 2) I'll open a hotfix PR to make the migration idempotent with leader-election lock and delay prune until replication confirmed.
jenni: Also add an audit alert: if kms:Decrypt denies occur for newly-migrated role names, create high-priority incident.
sec-bot: suggested-playbook: stopgap = temporary KMS allow for control-plane egress; persistent = migration lock + egress-ip stabilization + test that KMS calls succeed after alias promotion.
maria: I'll contact customer and request permission to add temp allowlist. tagging @ryan for exec.
ryan: On it. If customer says yes, ping ops for immediate change and post nonce in this thread.
alex.k: Followups: (a) add e2e test that verifies KMS decrypt from private control plane after any RBAC rename, (b) audit tool that cross-checks allowlist ACLs vs observed egress IPs.
jenni: assigning owners: ryan -> temp allowlist change, alex.k -> e2e test and migration PR review, maria -> customer comms & verify audit events, sec-bot -> create incident and run initial triage template.
maria: Thanks. I'll update here after customer response.
ryan: customer approved temporary KMS allow for IP 54.23.11.9 until 03/30. Ops applied change at 1719901205, they confirm decrypts now.
maria: Confirmed with customer — decrypts succeed, re-enabling services. We'll keep this thread as the audit trail.
ops-bot: note: change documented in infra-changes/1719901205-kms-allowlist-temp.json
maria: Filing follow-up checklist in SecurOps board: migration lock, egress-ip mapping, e2e test, alert rule. Closing in a few days after migration PR merges.
